name: Wide arpeggiated wave
description: the nocturne engine. One bass note, then the chord unfolding upward across an octave and a half: `Ab1e Eb3e Ab3e C4e Eb4e C4e Ab3e Eb3e`. The span from the bass to the top of the figure is 15–20 semitones; the *width* is the sound.

name: Bass note plus displaced chord
description: `Bb1q [F3,Bb3,D4]q [F3,Bb3,D4]q` in 3/4. The mazurka and waltz shape. The gap between the bass and the chord is the point; closing it makes it sound like a folk band.

name: Rocking tenths
description: `Ab1e C3e Ab1e C3e …`. A tenth apart, alternating. Warm and open, and the tenth is what makes it Romantic rather than an octave.

name: Sustained pedal bass under moving inner voices
description: `Ab1w // Eb3e F3e Gb3e F3e Eb3e F3e Gb3e F3e`. The bass holds for the whole bar while a middle voice moves. This is genuine two-voice left-hand writing and it is what most generated Chopin is missing.

name: Chromatic inner-voice descent
description: the bass stays, the note above it falls by semitone across four bars: `C3 → B2 → Bb2 → A2`. Chopin's most reliable way of making a repeated harmony feel like it is going somewhere.

name: Doubled octaves in the bass
description: `[Ab1,Ab2]h [Eb2,Eb3]h`. For weight at a climax, or for the ballades' declamatory passages. Rare and heavy; do not use it as a default.

name: Waltz oom-pah-pah, widely spaced
description: `Ab1q [C3,Eb3]q [C3,Eb3]q`. The textbook figure, but the bass is an octave lower than a Classical waltz would put it and the chord is thinner (two notes, not three).

name: Free arpeggio spanning the whole hand
description: `Db1e Ab1e F2e Ab2e Db3e F3e Ab3e Db4e`, a two-and-a-half-octave sweep in one bar. The barcarolle and the later nocturnes. Written as one gesture, pedalled through.

name: Repeated chord with a moving bass
description: the chord stays put while the bass walks underneath it: `Ab1e [C3,Eb3]e G1e [C3,Eb3]e F1e [C3,Eb3]e …`. Motion without any change in colour.

name: The left hand carries the melody
description: in the middle register, with the right hand accompanying above. Used for a return, or for the middle section of a nocturne. The tune sounds completely different an octave lower with a different attack, which is the reason to do it.

name: Silence under a cadenza
description: `rest_w`. The right hand runs free and the left hand simply stops. Chopin does this at every written-out ornamental flourish; keeping the accompaniment going through one is the surest way to make it sound mechanical.

name: Alberti bass
when_to_use: Simple support (stay out of melody's way)

name: Murky bass (octave alternation)
when_to_use: Simple support (stay out of melody's way)

name: Waltz bass (3/4, L:1/8)
when_to_use: Simple support (stay out of melody's way)

name: Written-out ornamental flourish
description: a cadenza-like run of small notes over a held or absent accompaniment, notated in real values (often 32nds or a burst of irregular groupings). Placed at a phrase's peak or before a return. The left hand usually stops.

name: The ornamented return
description: a melody comes back decorated rather than plain. This is Chopin's principal variation technique: same notes, more of them, arriving in a different order around the same anchors.

name: Appoggiatura sigh
description: a dissonance on the beat resolving down by step, slurred: `(Ab5q G5q)`. The core expressive gesture, and it should recur.

name: Rubato against a steady bass
description: the melody written with values that do not align evenly with the accompaniment: a triplet against duple, a quintuplet over four, dotted rhythms over even ones.

name: Chromatic passing motion inside a diatonic line
description: the melody steps through notes outside the key on its way between chord tones. Colour without modulation.

name: Long-breathed line
description: a phrase of eight or more bars that does not cadence in the middle. The line arches once and lands once.

name: Melodic leap of a sixth or seventh, filled in on the way back
description: the operatic gesture: an expressive upward leap, then a stepwise descent from it.

name: Repeated note with changing harmony beneath
description: the melody holds one pitch while the chord under it moves, so the same note means something different in each bar.

name: The melody in the tenor
description: the tune moves to the left hand's upper register with accompaniment above and below it. Used for a middle section or a transformed return.

name: Chromatic voice leading
description: inner voices sliding by semitone between chords that would otherwise be plain. The harmony is often simple; the *motion* between chords is the interest.

name: Enharmonic pivot
description: a diminished seventh or an augmented sixth respelled to land in a remote key. Chopin modulates further and faster than any of his contemporaries.

name: Neapolitan and augmented-sixth colour
description: at moments of pathos, especially in the mazurkas and nocturnes.

name: Modal inflection from Polish folk music
description: a raised fourth (Lydian) or a flattened seventh in the mazurkas, and drone fifths in the bass. This is what separates a mazurka from a waltz.

name: A dominant that refuses to resolve
description: the chord held, decorated, delayed over several bars before the tonic finally arrives.

name: Parallel diminished sevenths descending
description: a sequence of the same chord shape sliding down by semitone or minor third. Transitional, and it dissolves the key.

name: Ternary with an ornamented return
description: A, contrasting B, then A again with the melody decorated. The nocturne and mazurka default.

name: The coda that dissolves
description: the texture thins, the register rises or falls away, the dynamic drops to `pp` or `ppp`. Chopin rarely ends loudly.

name: Mazurka rhythm
description: the stress on beat 2 or 3 rather than 1, in 3/4. Written as a dotted or accented second beat. Without it a mazurka is a waltz.

name: Rhythmic dissolution before a return
description: the pulse becomes ambiguous through irregular groupings, then the return re-establishes it.

name: Bel canto phrasing marks
description: long slurs over whole phrases, not bar by bar. A slur that stops at the barline is not this idiom.
